caption: Between my dad's funeral loan and keeping my mom's lights on, R4 450 leaves before I've spent a cent on myself. Is this just what your forties look like too?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R24 000
p/m salary
Living in Witbank
slides.body:
Female, 45
Married, grown children
Job: Bookkeeper
Net salary: R24 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.includes: 3 bed in Del Judor, rates included
slides.body: Nearly paid off, which is the only reason the rest of this still balances.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Big shop plus my mother's top-ups
slides.body: Half of this trolley isn't for my own house anymore.

slides.title: Funeral loan repayment
slides.includes: R30 000 borrowed in February for my father's funeral, 18 months left
slides.body: I don't regret the loan. I do the sum in my head every payday.

slides.title: My mother's support
slides.includes: Her electricity, her groceries top-up, a caregiver two days a week
slides.body: Nobody asked me to do this in writing. I just started, and now it's a line item.

slides.title: Takeaways & comfort food
slides.includes: The nights since February I haven't wanted to cook
slides.body: I would have said R400. It's R950. Grief makes you order in more than you think.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Car instalment, petrol & insurance, medical aid, phone & fibre, electricity, my own funeral policy, stokvel
slides.body: R6 900 that has to run whether or not the year has been kind.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R24 000. Between the loan and my mother's account, R4 450 is gone before I've spent a cent on myself.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what care was costing me
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

Seeing my mother's support and the funeral loan on one screen was the first time I'd added them together.

No bank login needed.
